messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 18,000 km). That makes it about 2½ times larger than our own Jupiter, the biggest planet in the Solar System.

> *Key facts*  
> • **Mass**: ≈ 10–15 M_J (roughly 10–15 times Jupiter’s mass)  
> • **Radius**: ≈ 2.5 R_J  
> • **Orbit**: ~10 AU from its host star, still in the process of forming  

While there are other massive exoplanets—such as HD 106906 b (~11 M_J) and several “super‑Jupiters” with radii up to ~2 R_J—none exceed HD 100546 b in size. If future observations discover a planet larger than this, it would become the new record holder.
